lots.guide_summary: All AUD, no conversion. Nine SOLD hammers at Gowans Hobart in the last 11 months for the same Pro Hart small hand coloured etching series (close, different images): $130 (no glass) to $240, cluster $180 to $220. Two UNSOLD: the very same mask image passed in at Gowans in September 2026, and a nude AP passed in once before selling. No ASKING entries. Armitage past results could not be checked (web search budget exhausted).
lots.working: Keep: no SOLD for this exact image (the only same-image result passed in), so I used the lowest close SOLD in the series, $130 hammer (lot 384144), rather than the $180 framed cluster, to allow for this subject being less popular. $130 / 1.22 = $106.56, round down to $105 hammer ($128 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $180 hammer at Gowans (framed cluster), less about 17.5% seller commission and fees (about $32), $0 postage (local room) = $148; $148 / 2.44 = $60.66, round down to $60. Flip margin is thin and the same image just passed in, so KEEP only.
lots.confidence_reason: Signature read as stacked 'Pro / Hart' on enlargement and the image is matched to a Gowans lot catalogued as Pro Hart, so the identification is now credible. Many close SOLD entries (pages opened via the API, photos viewed), but none of this exact image, and the one same-image result passed in.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher's 372519 ($120, 'LTD EDN PRINT 302/1600'): dropped, photo shows an offset reproduction of an outback scene, a different kind of print. 411350 ($7, '3 PRO HART PRINTS'): dropped, job lot of low grade prints. 367214 ($440) and 385691 ($330): dropped from the guide, larger and more complex images, not comparable in size. Researcher's grouped '$220 to $440' entry split into individual verified lots. Unsold 432591 and 434175 ('PRO HART PRINT'): dropped, photos show offset outback reproductions. Feast or Fish 49/250 (432545, 434136): dropped, different kind. The researcher's doubt about attribution is withdrawn: the Gowans photo of the same image settles it as a catalogued Pro Hart.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged signature crop reads as a two-line 'Pro / Hart', matching the stacked signature on Gowans Pro Hart etchings. Pencil edition lower left, too faint to read (the Gowans copy reads about 4/50). Image matches Gowans lot 439005 exactly. Burr wood frame with cream mat, '5000' chalk mark on the glass or mount.
lots.condition: Framed and glazed, burr frame, mat and paper look clean in the photos. No foxing visible at this resolution. Back not photographed.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you read the edition number in pencil lower left and confirm the signature reads Pro Hart? Any foxing, staining or glass damage, and is there a gallery label or certificate on the back?

lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives. No sold, unsold or asking entry for a yellow-ground famille verte square vase was found. Web search budget was exhausted, so Armitage past results, Invaluable and dealer comparables were not checked; Gowans API searches (famille, famille verte, chinese yellow, square vase chinese, vase chinese) found nothing comparable.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence of the same item, so both maximum bids are 0.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark read (base not photographed), age unknown, no surviving comparables.
lots.dropped_entries: Gowans 384223 ($200, 19th century famille rose pen box, cracked): opened in the API JSON, dropped as a different form, palette and age. Gowans 418461 ($55, Chinese peacock signed vase): opened, dropped as a generic modern vase; the researcher's date was also wrong (listed 2026-06-21, not 2026-08-23). Gowans 431091 ($30, large Chinese painted vase, listed 2026-08-16): dropped, generic and not comparable.
lots.key_photo_findings: Crisp, even enamels with neat black outlines; yellow ground is uniform and bright, interior glaze very white and clean. The tidy, even finish and bright colours lean towards a 20th century (Republic or later) decorative piece rather than Kangxi-period work, but that cannot be settled without the base. No obvious chips at the rim in the photos.
lots.condition: Rim looks intact in the photos. Possible small marks on one panel, unclear. Base and interior depth not photographed.
lots.question_for_armitage: Please photograph or describe the base: is there a reign mark or seal, is the foot glazed or unglazed, and how worn is it? Any chips, cracks or restoration, and is there a lid (it is called a canister)?

lots.what_it_is: Monogram-print French bulldog key chain or bag charm, about 12.5 cm, studded collar, gold-tone chain and clip, in an orange box printed with a bulldog graphic and 'LOUIS VUITTON'. Very likely a replica or novelty, not a genuine Louis Vuitton product.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing found. Researcher found no entries; Gowans API searches for louis vuitton and vuitton charm return no lots, and web search budget was exhausted, so no genuine-LV comparables could be sought.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence and the item is very likely not genuine, so both maximum bids are 0.
lots.confidence_reason: No date code, heat stamp or hardware engraving visible; authenticity judged from design and packaging only, with no comparables.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crop shows oversized LV letters placed across the face, pyramid studs, and a box printed with a large monogram bulldog graphic. Genuine LV boxes are plain saffron with the name only, so the printed dog on the box is a strong replica sign. This bulldog design is a widely sold replica pattern. No serial or stamping visible.
lots.condition: Looks new or near new, box present.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there any heat stamp, date code or engraved hardware, and does it come with a receipt or dust bag? If not, assume it is a replica.
